mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.5% is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced discount rates on equity cash flows, as the Federal Reserve maintains an accommodative monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0%) signals economic weakness and delayed monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of the periods when UNRATE > 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by at least 0.5% from the prior month indicate robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by >=0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when HOUST and RSAFS both increase by >=0.5% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), the Federal Reserve sustains accommodative monetary policy, supporting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
regime_hint: low inflation and low rates regime
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when CPIAUCSL < 2.0% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 100) reflects robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% annualized (computed from GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS increase > 150k from prior month) indicates a healthy labor market, which increases consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when PAYEMS increase > 150k from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 0.5% from the prior month signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and produces positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of the periods when HOUST increases > 0.5% from prior month.
